liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ken Kesey interviewed by Frank Fey** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Kesey interview a fantastic highlight of the tape [8]
- **Ken Babbs and harmonica** (1 review): Ken Babbs plays loud harmonica [8]
- **The End** (1 review): On the last track a Prankster invites the Dead to sing; Garcia plugs in and says his voice is shot [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ken Kesey interviewed by Frank Fey**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Ken Babbs and harmonica**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Take Two: Ken Kesey**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Bull**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Peggy The Pistol**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **One-way Ticket**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Bells And Fairies**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Levitation**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-01-29.sbd.berger.99527.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 34 min; rated 3/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: The band doesn't seem to play background instruments on the tape; Kesey, Babbs and others supply vocals [7]

## Around the show

- Recording dates from 1966, a time when LSD was still legal [3]
- Track 10 features Jerry Garcia on vocals [12]
- Reviewer hears mostly Merry Pranksters talking and odd sounds from the acid test scene, not a Grateful Dead performance [13]
- Prankster calls them 'the Dead' only seven weeks after their first public gig under that name [7]
- Described as Acid Test 10 of 19, more defined than earlier Tests yet not over the top [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-01-29.sbd.berger.99527.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger; source: vinyl > 7" reel @ 7.5 ips [1]
